name: schema-annotation-invalid
description: An annotation attribute value does not follow the prefix:id value grammar or cites a source that has no row in the Sources section.
common_causes: A prefix was used in an annotation value but no row for it was added to the Prefixes section
The property part of the value was misspelled or was never added to the External annotations section
An external term such as foodonto:FOODON_00001234 was written bare instead of as the value of a mapping property
A dc:source value cites a source whose name has no row in the Sources section
A dc:source value cites a URL that is not under the link of any Sources row
The value of skos:exactMatch or skos:closeMatch was written as a bare identifier or a URL instead of in prefix notation
explanation: The value of an annotation attribute has the form 'prefix:id value': 'prefix:id' names a row of the External annotations section, whose 'prefix' is a row of the Prefixes section, and 'value' is that property's value. A link from a schema element to a term in an external ontology is written with a SKOS mapping property whose value is the external term in prefix notation, as in 'skos:exactMatch ncit:C25499' for the same concept or 'skos:closeMatch ncit:C25499' for one close enough to be used interchangeably in most applications; the prefix of that term must also be a row of the Prefixes section, while the term itself is not checked. A 'dc:source' value must name a row of the Sources section: the text either begins with a row's 'source' name or contains a URL that begins with a row's 'link' (compared without the scheme and without a trailing slash), and any other text such as 'Adapted from' is free. Four situations are flagged: (a) the prefix of the value is not a Prefixes row; (b) the 'prefix:id' is not an External annotations row, which is where a bare external term falls; (c) a 'dc:source' value names no Sources row; (d) the value of a mapping property has the form 'prefix:term' but its prefix is not a Prefixes row, or a mapping property's value is not in prefix notation at all. Every one of these is a warning and the schema still loads. The rows of a partnered library's standard schema count as the library's own, so a library partnered with the standard schema may use the standard's prefixes, external annotations, and sources without repeating them. The rules apply to standard schemas with versions 8.5.0 or later and to library schemas partnered with them; earlier schemas wrote bare external terms and are not checked.
correction_strategy: Write every annotation value as 'prefix:id value' with the prefix in the Prefixes section and the 'prefix:id' in the External annotations section, link an external term with skos:exactMatch or skos:closeMatch followed by the term in prefix notation, and make every dc:source value begin with a Sources row name or contain a URL under a Sources row link

correction_examples.explanation: Reason a: the prefix 'nowhere:' had no row in the Prefixes section; a defined prefix was used instead
Reason b: a bare external term is not an External annotations row; the term becomes the value of a SKOS mapping property
Reason c: the dc:source text named no Sources row; it now begins with the 'source' name of one
Reason d: the value of a mapping property must be an external term in prefix notation whose prefix is a Prefixes row

validation_hints: Check only schemas whose standard version (own or withStandard) is 8.5.0 or later; unpartnered libraries are not checked
The Sources, Prefixes, and External annotations rows of a partnered library's standard schema count as the library's own
Only dc:source values are checked against the Sources section
specification_reference: A.1.4.2. annotation; A.1.6. Schema sources; Appendix B SCHEMA_ANNOTATION_INVALID
